subtopics.title: Economic Growth — Meaning, Measurement and South Africa's Record

questions.question: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP:
options: Values output at constant prices, so only genuine extra output moves the number

questions.question: Nominal GDP rises 7% during 6% inflation. Real growth is roughly:
Over the past decade South Africa's real growth of about 1% against population growth of about 1,5% means:
options: Real GDP per capita has been falling — the average person is slowly getting poorer
Real GDP per capita has been rising fast

questions.question: The doubling arithmetic in the lesson says an economy growing at 5% doubles in about 14 years, while at 1% it takes about:

subtopics.title: Measuring Inequality — the Lorenz Curve and the Gini Coefficient

questions.question: On the Lorenz diagram, the horizontal axis measures:
options: The cumulative percentage of the population, arranged from poorest to richest

questions.question: South Africa's Lorenz curve passes through the point where 60% of people hold only about:
The Gini coefficient equals the area between the diagonal and the Lorenz curve divided by:
options: The whole area under the diagonal

questions.question: Wealth is a stock and income is a flow. In South Africa the wealth stock is even more concentrated than income, with the top tenth estimated to hold:
options: About a quarter of all wealth

subtopics.title: Redistribution — the Methods Governments Actually Use

questions.question: The defining test of a progressive tax is that higher earners pay:
options: More rands in total, whatever the rate
The same rate as everyone else
A larger percentage of their income

questions.question: Maize meal and brown bread are zero-rated because a uniform VAT would otherwise:
options: Absorb a larger fraction of a poor household's budget than a rich one's

questions.question: South Africa's social grant system pays out monthly to approximately:
A no-fee school and a free basic water allocation redistribute income because:
options: They are paid for by the household later
Every service received free is money the household keeps — income by another route
They replace the need for taxation
They are forms of progressive taxation

subtopics.title: Achieving Growth, the Constraints in the Way, and Standard of Living

questions.question: The 'padlock' sentence pairs each South African constraint with a growth source it blocks. Load shedding and underperforming freight rail padlock:
options: The physical capacity to produce — reliable inputs for production

questions.question: Unfilled vacancies existing alongside unemployment above 30% is evidence of:
options: A skills mismatch between what schools produce and what firms need

questions.question: Which statement about real GDP per capita as a living-standards measure is FALSE?
options: It is silent on how income is distributed
It fully captures unpaid household work and informal activity
It counts polluting output as gain while ignoring the damage
It measures money rather than health or learning

subtopics.title: The Pot and the People — Growth Done Honestly

questions.question: The 'price trick' makes the pot look bigger when:
options: The money value rises purely because prices rose
The pot is measured at last year's prices

questions.question: The pot grows 2% while the crowd around it grows 3%. The average plate:
Without a growing pot, helping the poor can only happen by:
options: Taking from one plate to fill another — which works but has limits

subtopics.title: The Queue of One Hundred — Seeing Inequality Without a Graph

questions.question: Walking the real South African queue, your coin count at person 60 stands at about:
The avalanche at the end of the walk happens because the final 10 people hold roughly:
A Gini coefficient of zero would describe a queue where:
options: Every step of the walk adds exactly one coin — perfect equality
Only half the queue holds coins
The queue has no coins at all

questions.question: The wealth queue is more lopsided than the income queue because:
options: Stocks accumulate across generations — and the law once barred most South Africans from accumulating

subtopics.title: Moving Coins Along the Queue — and Growing the Pot at the Same Time

questions.question: The top step of South Africa's income tax staircase takes:
Which move targets the size of TOMORROW'S coins rather than today's?
options: Making township and rural schools genuinely good — moving skills

questions.question: Taxing 'the cooks' too brutally risks:
options: Investment leaving and taking jobs with it
A lower Gini with no side effects

questions.question: The lesson's closing position is that growth and redistribution:
options: Must be traded off — a country picks exactly one
Are the same policy under two names
Fund and feed each other — policy's craft is keeping both moving at once
